headline: Coal-Fired Power Plants Can Change Rainfall Patterns, 15-Year Study Says
caption: Reports a study by Wolfgang Junkermann and Jorg Hacker (Bulletin of the American Meteorological Society), whose research aircraft flew downwind of power stations in dozens of countries: modern coal plants, through their filter systems, emit more ultrafine particles than road traffic. The particles add condensation nuclei and can shift rainfall locally and regionally, perhaps even intensify rain.
alt: Screen grab of the Weather Channel article 'Coal-Fired Power Plants Can Change Rainfall Patterns, 15-Year Study Says'.

headline: Kohlekraftwerke – kleine „Wettermaschinen“ (Teil 1)
caption: The German weather service explains that beyond their CO₂, coal power stations change today’s weather locally: the warm, saturated air from the cooling towers forms plumes, can break through inversions above low fog, and on calm frosty days can even let ‘industrial snow’ fall near the plant.
alt: Screen grab of the DWD Thema des Tages 'Kohlekraftwerke – kleine Wettermaschinen (Teil 1)', 5 February 2018.
credit: Markus Übel, Deutscher Wetterdienst, Thema des Tages

headline: Kohlekraftwerke – kleine „Wettermaschinen“ (Teil 2)
caption: In unstable, showery air the cooling-tower plume can act as a ‘trigger’ for showers. Radar images of 2 February 2018 and 8 December 2017 show showers starting at, strengthening at and lining up behind the Niederaußem power station near Cologne.
alt: Screen grab of the DWD Thema des Tages 'Kohlekraftwerke – kleine Wettermaschinen (Teil 2)', 6 February 2018.
credit: Markus Übel, Deutscher Wetterdienst, Thema des Tages

headline: The floods caused by heavy rainfall in Germany and Belgium – increase of heavy rainfall under climate change
caption: JAXA’s satellite rain data (GSMaP, GPM) show that western Germany and Belgium received more than 75 mm in three days, 12–14 July 2021, about as much as a normal July brings in a whole month. JAXA links such extremes to the IPCC’s finding (AR6, 2021) that heavy rainfall is becoming more frequent and intense, and calls for continued observation from space.
alt: Screen grab of the JAXA Earth-graphy article on the July 2021 floods in Germany and Belgium, with a satellite rainfall map of Europe.
credit: JAXA Earth Observation Research Center, Earth-graphy
